comments.body: Sorry for the confusion: that part of the docstring is describing numpy's behavior, not JAX's behavior (look for *original docstring below*). JAX specifically avoids promotion to float64 in many places where numpy does so, so I think this is working as intended. But the documentation should probably be updated to reflect this – are you interested in sending a fix?
I'll just close this.  It's not too important to me.  I just thought it was weird 😄
Also, just curious, but when you implement the Array API, will you be ditching the functions (like `float_power`) that aren't part of it?  (I'm happy just sticking to the Array API interface.)

I'm not sure what you mean by Array API, but the `jax.numpy` interface is designed to match what is in `numpy`. So we probably wouldn't deprecate/remove any functionality unless it were deprecated/removed in NumPy itself.

@jakevdp I mean this: https://data-apis.org/array-api/latest/.  Numpy added `numpy.array_api`, so I assumed that Jax would eventually follow suit?  This would allow library code to be written in a way that supports all libraries that implement the Array API.  For example, my efax library would support jax, numpy, pytorch, etc.

Oh, right, I've seen the discussions around that in the NumPy forums. I don't know of any concrete plans to implement that in JAX at the moment, but it looks like it would make sense. Though it's pretty clear that JAX can't support the entirety of the Array API as currently proposed: for example, it allows for mutation of data buffers, which is not possible in JAX.

> Though it's pretty clear that JAX can't support the entirety of the Array API as currently proposed: for example, it allows for mutation of data buffers, which is not possible in JAX.

I don't totally understand what they promise.  They did discuss Jax here: https://data-apis.org/array-api/latest/design_topics/copies_views_and_mutation.html.  It appears to be discussed here: https://github.com/data-apis/array-api/issues/24
Oh, I was just referring to the fact that `__setitem__` is listed as one of the operations in the Array API. This is a mutating operation that JAX can't support.

> Oh, I was just referring to the fact that __setitem__ is listed as one of the operations in the Array API. This is a mutating operation that JAX can't support.

I understand, but this is discussed in the linked thread.  Stephen had some ideas on how to make it work in this comment: https://github.com/data-apis/array-api/issues/24#issuecomment-682092006

I see, thanks for the link. In my mind it would be clearer to just have attempted mutation raise an error as JAX currently does.

In any case, I'll reiterate that I don't know of any concrete efforts to add Array API compatiblity to JAX, and even if we were to do that some day, I doubt we'd drop existing functionality in the `jax.numpy` interface (just as I doubt numpy itself would ever deprecate or remove those legacy APIs)

issue.body:
### Description

```python
import jax.numpy as jnp
x = jnp.ones(1)
jnp.float_power(x, x).dtype  # float32!
```
Violates the documented behaviour: https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_autosummary/jax.numpy.float_power.html:
> This differs from the power function in that integers, float16, and float32 are promoted to floats with a minimum precision of float64 so that the result is always inexact.
issue.title: jax.numpy.float_power doesn't promote dtype as specified
